title: Section-normalized abelian coefficient-tower presentation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $T$. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ be the varying-coefficient tower category of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], and $B_\bullet$ its commutative-ring sheaf tower of [def-sp-commutative-coefficient-ring-tower]; Lean index $n$ means coefficient exponent $n+1$. Use the strict semilinear systems, their level evaluations, canonical scalar assignments and normalized tensor coherence of [def-pur-system-level-left-extension-basic]. Given an equivalence $e:\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)\simeq\operatorname{StrictRingSystem}(B_\bullet)$, define $\operatorname{spCoefficientEvaluation}(e,n)$ to be $e$ followed by evaluation at $n$. Define $\operatorname{SpCoefficientTowersAbelian}(\ell,E,T)$ to be the structure with: an equivalence $e$ as above whose section modules, vertical restrictions, every iterated transition and every morphism component agree with those of the product-site presentation; additivity of $e$; Grothendieck abelianness [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] of the tower category; preservation of finite limits and finite colimits by every evaluation and preservation of each small filtered colimit by every evaluation; an ordinary unbounded derived-category localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; a canonical scalar assignment and its normalized tensor coherence; natural ordinary reduction maps $\mathrm{ev}_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m\to\mathrm{ev}_m$ for every $m\leq n$, equal to the tensor adjuncts of the strict transitions; and derived reductions $\mathbf L(-\otimes_{B_n}B_m)\circ D(\mathrm{ev}_n)\to D(\mathrm{ev}_m)$. On every complex the derived reduction is the composite of the derived-evaluation comparison, the recorded scalar-model comparison, localization of the ordinary reduction, and the inverse target-evaluation comparison. Equal-index reductions are the recorded derived unitors, and successive reductions equal direct reduction under the recorded derived tensor associator. All data and equations are retained; this structure definition does not assert that it is inhabited. For $T:\operatorname{Scheme}^{t}$ and $E:\operatorname{Type}^{u}$ the coefficient universe is $\max(u,t+1)$ and the derived-category universe is its successor.
